questions.prompt: Which letter should be temporarily excluded after it is appended?

choices.label: The least frequent remaining letter.
choices.feedback: Holding out the previous letter prevents equal neighboring characters while allowing it to be used again later.

choices.label: The letter just appended.
choices.feedback: Holding out the previous letter prevents equal neighboring characters while allowing it to be used again later.

choices.label: Every letter that has already appeared anywhere.
choices.feedback: Holding out the previous letter prevents equal neighboring characters while allowing it to be used again later.

questions.prompt: Among the allowed letters, which should the heap prefer?

choices.label: The one with the most occurrences remaining.
choices.feedback: Using the most frequent available letter avoids leaving too many copies of it to separate later.

choices.label: The one earliest in the alphabet regardless of its count.
choices.feedback: Using the most frequent available letter avoids leaving too many copies of it to separate later.

choices.label: The one with the fewest occurrences remaining.
choices.feedback: Using the most frequent available letter avoids leaving too many copies of it to separate later.

questions.prompt: When may the held-out letter become available again?

choices.label: Immediately before choosing the next letter.
choices.feedback: One different intervening letter is enough to separate two occurrences of the held-out letter.

choices.label: Only after every other letter is exhausted.
choices.feedback: One different intervening letter is enough to separate two occurrences of the held-out letter.

choices.label: After a different letter has been appended.
choices.feedback: One different intervening letter is enough to separate two occurrences of the held-out letter.
